title: India's edible oil import bill rises 24% to record ₹2 trillion in 2025-26
description:
India's edible oil imports rose 6 per cent to 16.92 million tonnes in the oil year ended October 2026, and the import bill jumped 24 per cent to about Rs 200,000 crore, the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) said on Monday.
Edible oil imports in the 2025-26 oil year (November-October) increased compared with 16.01 million tonnes a year earlier, when the bill was about Rs 161,126 crore, the trade body said in a statement.
Total vegetable oil imports, including non-edible oils, rose 5 per cent to 17.24 million tonnes from 16.36 million tonnes.
India imports edible oils to bridge the gap between domestic supply and demand, a practice that began in the 1990s. Over the past 20 years, import volumes have risen 2.8 times, while the cost has risen nearly 15 times, SEA said.
